problem: Navigation skills (VLN, ObjectNav, PointNav, SocialNav, human following, EQA) are evaluated in isolated single-task benchmarks, mostly with shortest-path trajectories and a single robot morphology. This does not test whether 'unified' models can switch between skills within one episode or generalize across embodiments.
motivation: Real deployment needs agents to chain diverse behaviors in one episode, deal with moving humans, and work on different robot bodies. Shortest-path demonstrations also miss human behaviors such as exploratory glances, hesitation and anticipatory avoidance. A benchmark that composes tasks, covers multiple embodiments and uses human teleoperated demonstrations is needed to expose these gaps.
key_idea: OmniNavBench is an Isaac Sim benchmark of composite instructions that chain at least two of VLN, ObjectNav, PointNav and HumanFollow, with SocialNav and EQA as concurrent constraints. It covers wheeled, quadruped and humanoid robots and provides human-teleoperated expert trajectories.
insight: Unified models reach moderate sub-goal progress (SGC up to 44.54) but almost never complete full episodes (SR mostly below 2%), so sequential coordination is the bottleneck rather than isolated skills. The OSR-vs-SR gap (Uni-NaVid on Aliengo: 26.47 OSR vs 1.96 SR) shows failures in termination decisions. Failure modes differ by embodiment (H1 falls in 60-80% of failures) and performance drops on Matterport3D scans. Performance shifts noticeably with instruction style (OmniNav SR 8.74 -> 14.47 with First Person), indicating brittleness to phrasing.
method: Composite task specification: a mission M = {(l_i, tau_i, g_i)} is an ordered chain of at least 2 sub-tasks from VLN (including Return), ObjectNav, PointNav and HumanFollow, with SocialNav and EQA superimposed as parallel constraints. Difficulty ranges from 2 to 4+ sub-tasks (39% / 32% / 29%).

Human teleoperation data: trained operators drive the robots in Isaac Sim, and experts verify egocentric video. This yields 1,779 trajectories (avg 16.7 m, 48.9 s, 24 h, 2.6M RGB-D frames) stored as morphology-agnostic waypoints (x, y, theta, t); low-level actions are excluded.

Simulation platform: Isaac Sim with full physics and RL locomotion controllers from VLN-PE, three robots (Carter, Aliengo, H1), and waypoint, velocity or discrete action interfaces. Sensors are configurable (RGB, depth, panoramic, LiDAR, IMU), and dynamic pedestrians (1-2 per episode, 1.0 m/s, deterministic) come from omni.anim.people.
Scenes and splits: 170 scenes (85 Matterport3D, 61 GRScenes-Home, 24 GRScenes-Commercial). Split by scene into 1,187 train trajectories (112 scenes) and 592 test trajectories (58 scenes).
Instruction stylization: Qwen3-Max generates Concise, First Person and Verbose paraphrases with manual verification, giving 7,116 instructions.

Metrics: SR (stop within 2.0 m of the final goal), CSR, SGC (continuous per-sub-task progress), OSR, SPL, HFS, HFR, EQA-ACC, and SII (fraction of steps within 1.2 m of a human). Distances are NavMesh geodesic for VLN/ObjectNav and Euclidean otherwise.

setting.backbone: Benchmark paper; evaluates MTU3D, PoliFormer, Uni-NaVid and OmniNav zero-shot with released weights
setting.training_data: none for the evaluated models (released weights, zero-shot); the benchmark supplies 1,187 training trajectories that were not used in the reported experiments
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (camera count, resolution and FOV adapted per model); optional panoramic, LiDAR, IMU
setting.action_space: waypoint sequences, velocity commands (v, omega), or discrete forward/turn actions mapped to physical motion; RL locomotion controllers
setting.privileged: none for agents; a small sim-vs-real qualitative check with Uni-NaVid on a wheeled robot exists in the appendix

numbers_note: Only 5 of the 12 model-embodiment rows in Tab. main_results are listed (a subset of baseline evaluations, not the paper's own method). Others include the H1 rows (OmniNav SR 0.00, Uni-NaVid SR 1.06), as well as the instruction-style ablation in Tab. styletest (e.g. OmniNav First Person SR 14.47, SPL 11.88).
results: All four unified models (MTU3D, PoliFormer, Uni-NaVid, OmniNav) perform poorly on composite episodes: best SR is 8.74 (OmniNav on Aliengo) and most configurations are below 2%. SGC reaches 44.54 (Uni-NaVid, Aliengo) and OSR 26.47, showing that progress and goal-reaching happen without correct completion. Human following (best HFS 45.16) and social safety are also weak, and performance varies with embodiment, scene type and instruction style.
limitations: Only four models are evaluated zero-shot; no model is trained on the provided training split, so the benefit of the human demonstrations is untested.

Success rates near zero limit discrimination between methods; the dataset is modest in size (592 test trajectories), and some findings (e.g., embodiment effects) are partly explained rather than causally tested.
Simulation only, apart from a qualitative sim-to-real check; pedestrians follow scripted paths and instruction variants come from an LLM.
